title: A GIFT FOR THE LEADER, LAST OF ALL

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When they had finished dividing the land into its allotted portions, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them, as the Lord had commanded. They gave him the town he asked for—Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim. And he built up the town and settled there. These are the territories that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the tribal clans of Israel assigned by lot at Shiloh in the presence of the Lord at the entrance to the tent of meeting. And so they finished dividing the land - Josh 19:49-51 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After every tribe has received its portion, at the very end, Joshua is given his own inheritance. Notice the order: the leader is served last. Joshua, who had faithfully overseen the distribution of land to everyone else, does not grab the best portion first or use his position to secure special advantage. He waits until all the people are settled, and only then receives a single town that he humbly asks for.

This is a portrait of servant leadership. Joshua's greatness is shown not in claiming privilege but in putting the people's needs before his own. He led the whole nation into its inheritance and took his own share last of all. There is deep humility in a leader who ensures everyone else is provided for before considering himself.

And so, the passage tells us, "they finished dividing the land." The long task begun chapters earlier is complete. Every tribe has its portion, assigned by lot before the Lord at the entrance to the tent of meeting. What God had promised Abraham centuries before was now fully parcelled out to his descendants. God finishes what He begins.

Joshua points us, as he so often does, to the greater Joshua — Jesus. For our Lord came not to be served but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many (Mark 10:45). Jesus, though He was Lord of all, took the lowest place, washing His disciples' feet and laying down His life for us. He secured our eternal inheritance before receiving His own glory, putting our need before His comfort at infinite cost. Joshua taking his portion last is a faint but beautiful shadow of the Servant King who gave everything for His people. And in Him, we who deserved nothing receive an inheritance that will never fade.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you use whatever influence you have to serve others or to secure advantage?
- How does Joshua's example of taking his portion last challenge you?
- How does Jesus, the Servant King, deepen your gratitude for your inheritance in Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You took the lowest place and served us at infinite cost, securing our inheritance before Your own glory. Give me a servant heart like Yours, and thank You for the inheritance I have in You. Amen.
